name: Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem Ltd
title: Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem Ltd - 543321 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue INR1,671m (+43% YoY) on volume, with management reiterating 25-30% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, while a new INR200 crore greenfield site is being built as Dahej nears saturation.

triggers.label: Electrolyte revenue hit by raw material shortage

summary.headline: Tatva Chintan Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 43% YoY to INR1,671 million, with EBITDA up 86% YoY to INR323 million.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR1,671 million grew 43% YoY and 25% QoQ, and EBITDA of INR323 million rose 86% YoY and 15% QoQ. Growth was led by volume rather than price, with price pass-on only starting about 40-50 days before the call. Electrolyte Salts was the weak spot, down 52% QoQ to INR63 million after raw material shortages linked to the Middle East crisis halted production for several weeks. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25-30% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, and announced a greenfield facility of about INR200 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Pharma & Agro Intermediates and Specialty Chemicals revenue

segments.name: Phase Transfer Catalysts (PTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR428 million, up 47% YoY and 38% QoQ. Management said rising PTC demand is partly absorbed by forward integration into SDA and Electrolyte Salts, so less PTC is sold externally over time.

segments.name: Structure Directing Agents (SDA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR578 million, up 47% YoY and 10% QoQ. Euro 7 implementation has started to convert into revenue; management expects geographic rollout over 3-5 years, with the Europe-led demand easing Euro 6 limits.

segments.name: Pharma & Agro Intermediates and Specialty Chemicals (PASC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR584 million, up 25% YoY and 63% QoQ. Repeat orders on recently commercialised molecules; one pharma intermediate entered commercial production in Q1, and more pharma molecules are expected in the second half.

segments.name: Electrolyte Salts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR63 million (management cited about INR6 crore in the Q&A), down 52% QoQ on raw material shortages. Hybrid battery customer commercialisation expected from October-November 2026, with full-scale commercialisation in late 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at 25-30%, and management said the Q1 quarterly run-rate should be maintained.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 20-22%, after Q1 came in at a lower margin.
Pharma molecules: INR70-80 crore revenue from the three new molecules in FY27, rising to about INR200 crore at full utilisation.
Electrolyte Salts: FY27 revenue guidance of INR40-60 crore (about 10% of revenue) retained.
Long-term: at least 20-25% CAGR over the next 3-4 years, with about 20-22% post-tax ROIC targeted.
Semiconductor commercialisation not expected before Q4 2028.
capex_capacity: Board approved a new greenfield facility of about INR200 crore; groundbreaking was scheduled for 20 July 2026.
New site is multipurpose and fungible across pharma, agro, electrolytes and SDA. Expected peak revenue about INR300 crore at 1.2-1.5x asset turn.
Target commissioning within 21 months, internally 18 months.
Dahej is nearly saturated; only a small debottlenecking block of 4-6 reactors is feasible. Current capacity is about INR800-850 crore of revenue at peak.
Continuous flow chemistry: 2 commercial products use it today; about 7-8 products in pilot or commercial phase are expected to use it.
MONOGLYME plant equipment was repurposed for a supercapacitor electrolyte raw material; glyme capacity expansion is on hold due to Chinese price pressure.
demand_pricing: Price increases are only starting to be passed on, from roughly 40-50 days before the call. Management said most of the Q1 growth was volume-driven and that prior cost increases were not fully passed on, which hit margins.
Electrolyte Salts volumes were limited by key raw material shortages from the Middle East crisis, causing the business to sit idle for several weeks.
Management said there is no order book; demand is visible quarter to quarter.

Semiconductor: first plant-scale commercial batch delivered and qualified by an MNC intermediary for the most stringent application, the key starting block for semiconductors. Management expects 3-4 plant-scale trials over the next 2 years, and 5 products are in its semiconductor pipeline.
Chinese anti-involution policy: subsidy and VAT rollback is reported but not law, with possible effect from January 2027; management sees potential benefit for Indian specialty chemical players.
Euro 7 is currently only in Europe, with US, Japan, China and India to follow over 3-5 years. Chinese SDA demand is yet to recover, while rest-of-world demand is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 guidance be achieved, and what is the biggest execution risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no obstacles, since customer demand and segment demand are visible.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue do the three new pharma molecules add, and what is their full-utilisation potential?
qa_highlights.answer: INR70-80 crore of revenue in FY27, rising next year, and about INR200 crore at full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the greenfield capex for, what revenue will it generate, and when will it be in place?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a multipurpose facility for scaling R&D-ready products and domestic demand, with about INR300 crore of revenue at peak. Target commissioning is 18-21 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Electrolyte Salts reach 10% of revenue, and how will it scale from INR6 crore to INR60 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management retained the INR40-60 crore FY27 guidance, said capacity is in place, and said there is no firm order book, only quarterly visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stays with 20-22% for the year after a lower-margin Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Dahej have room for more capacity, and when will the new site be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej is nearly saturated; only a small debottlenecking block is feasible. Management expects stagnation from next year without the new site.

risks_watch: Raw material supply disruption (Middle East crisis) for Electrolyte Salts; the business was idle for several weeks in Q1.
Margin recovery depends on passing on raw material cost increases, which only started about 40-50 days before the call.
Chinese price competition in glymes and MONOGLYME; capacity expansion has been put on hold.
Pace of semiconductor qualification (3-4 plant-scale trials over 2 years); commercialisation not expected before Q4 2028.
Hybrid battery customer ramp-up (October-November 2026 start, full scale late 2027) and the pharma molecule ramp in H2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand visibility and the new capacity plan, with guidance reiterated. Management was cautious and candid on Electrolyte Salts raw material disruption, the timing of semiconductor commercialisation, and the limited price pass-through so far. Some answers were vague or deferred, such as the China policy and the order book.
key_quotes: Customer demands are very crystal clear, very highly visible.
We consider this to be one of the Tatva Chintan's glaring achievements of the past decade.
So most of this is genuinely a volume growth and not a pricing differential.

adds.what: Greenfield multipurpose facility (pharma, agro, electrolytes, SDA) at about INR200 crore capex
Small debottlenecking block of 4-6 reactors at Dahej

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth held at 25-30% (midpoint 27.5%) with Q1 revenue +43% YoY; backing is partial: INR70-80 crore from three new pharma molecules, Electrolyte Salts guide of INR40-60 crore, and a INR200 crore greenfield site 21 months out, but management said there is no order book.
